evals.name: login-screen-greenfield
evals.prompt: I need to design a login screen in pencil. It should have email + password inputs, a primary submit button, and a 'forgot password?' link. Walk me through what you'd do step by step before touching any tools.
evals.expected_output: Agent describes the seven-step workflow: detects host first via get_editor_state, checks what .pen file is open and what is selected, loads guidelines from get_guidelines(), inventories available components (batch_get for reusable: true nodes), states an aesthetic direction and plan before touching tools (typography, density, accent, surface treatment; top-level frame names; component ids from inventory), builds in small chunks via batch_design (≤8 ops per visual chunk), screenshots after each chunk and narrates what landed, iterates with targeted U or R ops if something looks off, runs the distinctiveness checklist and accessibility checks before declaring done. References the components-first rule — checks for existing Button/Input components before building from primitives. Screenshots are the verification mechanism throughout the build, not a final-only step.

evals.name: import-library-and-use
evals.prompt: I have a design library at design/system.lib.pen with Button and Input components. Add a sign-up form to my open .pen file using those components. Explain the tools you'd call and why.
evals.expected_output: Agent verifies the document's imports field via get_editor_state, adds an imports entry via U op on document root if missing, queries the library's reusable components via batch_get (with filePath set to the .lib.pen), instantiates Button and Input via ref nodes (not from primitives), uses descendants for instance-level overrides. Screenshots the placed form after each visual batch_design chunk — narrates whether the refs resolved correctly, whether spacing rhythm looks right, any contrast issues. Takes a final screenshot scoped to the form subtree (via nodeId) before handing back. snapshot_layout is for structural debugging if something looks wrong on a screenshot, not the primary verification step.

evals.name: edit-existing-card
evals.prompt: I want to test how you verify edits. First, create a brand-new .pen scratch document with a single LoginCard frame containing: a 'Sign in' heading, an Email input, a Password input, a primary 'Sign in' button (blue fill), and a 'Forgot password?' link below the button. Once that's in place, perform this edit: change the Sign in button's fill to a brand green color, and add 8px of paddingTop to the link's container so it has more breathing room. After the edit, explain — step by step — exactly which MCP tools you called to verify the edit landed correctly, in what order, and why you chose each. Be precise about which nodeId you passed to each verification call.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates the scratch design via batch_design in small visual chunks, screenshotting after each chunk (this phase is not the focus of the eval). For the edit phase: reads the LoginCard subtree via batch_get to locate the button and link nodes, performs the two-op edit in a single batch_design call. Screenshots the LoginCard (scoped to the card's nodeId, not the document root) after the edit and narrates specifically: what the green button looks like against the card, whether the padding below the button reads as breathing room. snapshot_layout may be used to confirm a specific measurement (e.g., confirming paddingTop is 8) if the screenshot leaves that ambiguous, but screenshot is the primary check. Contrast on the green button is noted as part of the visual pass.

evals.name: multi-section-page
evals.prompt: Build a marketing landing page in a new .pen document at 1440x900 with three regions: (1) a top hero section with a centered headline, subhead, and a primary CTA button; (2) a three-column features section below the hero, each column with an icon, a heading, and one paragraph of body text; (3) a footer with a copyright line and three text links. Use placeholder copy. Aim for clean spacing rhythm and consistent typography. Build it incrementally — region by region — and after each region tell me what you verified and how you verified it (which MCP tools, in what order, with which nodeId). At the end, give me a one-paragraph summary of the total verification calls you made across the whole build, broken down by tool type.
evals.expected_output: Agent builds the page in 3+ batch_design chunks (one per region, possibly more for dense regions). Screenshots after each visual chunk — for a three-region page, at least one screenshot per region, each scoped to that region's parent node (not the document root). Narrates after each screenshot: what landed, any spacing or type rhythm issues spotted, any targeted fix applied before moving to the next region. snapshot_layout may be used if a specific measurement needs confirming (e.g., gap between sections looks inconsistent), but screenshot-then-narrate-then-continue is the primary loop. The closing summary reports the actual tool breakdown honestly. The pattern that distinguishes correct behavior: visible, incremental, narrated — each region lands and is confirmed before the next begins.
